claim: CaMKII is a dodecameric holoenzyme.
source: CaMKII is unusual among protein kinases because it is organized into a dodecameric holoenzyme (Bennett et al., 1983; Woodgett et al., 1983; Kolodziej et al., 2000; Morris and Torok, 2001; Rosenberg et al., 2005; Chao et al., 2011; see Stratton et al., 2013 for a recent review of CaMKII structure, shown schematically in Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior structural studies and referenced in Figure 1A.

claim: The CaMKII holoenzyme consists of a central hub formed by the association of C-terminal domains.
source: The holoenzyme consists of a central hub formed by the association of the C-terminal domains of CaMKII, to which the catalytic modules, consisting of the kinase domain and a regulatory segment, are attached by a variable linker (see Figure 1B for a schematic representation of the domains of CaMKII).
evidence: Described in text and illustrated in Figure 1B showing domain architecture.

claim: There are four CaMKII genes in humans (α, β, γ, and δ).
source: There are four CaMKII genes in humans, termed α, β, γ, and δ and these generate ∼40 isoforms through alternative splicing that results in variations in the linker (Tombes et al., 2003).
evidence: Stated explicitly with citation to Tombes et al., 2003.

claim: The α and β isoforms of CaMKII are found predominantly in neurons.
source: The α and β isoforms are found predominantly in neurons, while the γ and δ isoforms are distributed more broadly.
evidence: Explicitly stated tissue distribution of isoforms.

claim: Human CaMKIIα has a 30-residue linker connecting the catalytic module to the hub domain.
source: In this paper we focus on the human α isoform, CaMKIIα, the major isoform in neurons, which has a 30-residue linker connecting the catalytic module to the hub domain.
evidence: Explicitly stated structural feature of the construct studied.

claim: The regulatory segment of autoinhibited CaMKII docks within the substrate-recognition groove of the kinase domain and keeps it inactive.
source: The regulatory segment of autoinhibited CaMKII docks within the substrate-recognition groove of the kinase domain and keeps it inactive (Hook and Means, 2001).
evidence: Stated with citation to Hook and Means, 2001.

claim: An increase in calcium levels results in the binding of Ca2+/calmodulin to the regulatory segment, thereby activating CaMKII.
source: An increase in calcium levels results in the binding of Ca2+/calmodulin (Ca2+/CaM) to the regulatory segment, thereby activating CaMKII (Figure 1C; Colbran et al., 1989; Ikura et al., 1992).
evidence: Stated with citations and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: CaMKII has no phosphorylation sites within the activation loop.
source: In contrast to most other kinases, CaMKII has no phosphorylation sites within the activation loop.
evidence: Explicitly stated as a distinguishing feature of CaMKII.

claim: Thr 286 is a critical phosphorylation site located in the R1 element of the regulatory segment.
source: A critical phosphorylation site, Thr 286, is located in the R1 element of the regulatory segment (see Figure 1B; the residue numbering we use corresponds to that of a human CaMKIIα construct in which the 30-residue linker between the catalytic module and the hub domain is deleted [Chao et al., 2011]).
evidence: Stated explicitly with reference to Figure 1B and citation.

claim: The phosphorylation of Thr 286 requires one activated kinase domain to phosphorylate another kinase domain in the same holoenzyme.
source: The phosphorylation of Thr 286 requires one activated kinase domain to phosphorylate another kinase domain in the same holoenzyme, and trans-phosphorylation between different holoenzymes is not observed (Hanson et al., 1994; Rich and Schulman, 1998).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: Phosphorylation of Thr 286 prevents the R1 element from rebinding to the kinase domain, thereby conferring partial calcium-independence to the catalytic module.
source: Phosphorylation of Thr 286 prevents the R1 element from rebinding to the kinase domain, thereby conferring partial calcium-independence to the catalytic module (Lou et al., 1986; Lisman et al., 2002).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: Mutant mice with Thr 286 in CaMKIIα replaced by alanine have limited LTP generation and display impairments in learning and memory.
source: Mutant mice with Thr 286 in CaMKIIα replaced by alanine have limited LTP generation and display impairments in learning and memory (Giese et al., 1998).
evidence: Stated with citation to Giese et al., 1998.

claim: Thr 305 and Thr 306 are key phosphorylation sites located within the calmodulin-binding portion of the regulatory segment.
source: Two other key sites of phosphorylation, Thr 305 and Thr 306, are located within the calmodulin-binding portion of the regulatory segment, in the R3 element.
evidence: Explicitly stated location of phosphorylation sites.

claim: Phosphorylation of Thr 305 or Thr 306 weakens the affinity of CaMKII for Ca2+/CaM.
source: Phosphorylation of either residue weakens the affinity of CaMKII for Ca2+/CaM (Hanson and Schulman, 1992; Colbran, 1993).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: Activation of the CaMKII holoenzyme enables CaMKII subunits to exchange between different holoenzymes.
source: Using in vitro experimentation, we now report that activation of the CaMKII holoenzyme enables CaMKII subunits to exchange between different holoenzymes and to spread their state of activation in the process.
evidence: Main finding of the study stated in the introduction.

claim: Samples derived from the same CaMKII holoenzyme preparation showed both six-fold and seven-fold symmetry when visualized by electron microscopy and X-ray crystallography.
source: The experiments on CaMKII that we report here were prompted by a curious observation concerning the stoichiometry of subunits in CaMKII, which was that samples derived from the same CaMKII holoenzyme preparation showed both six-fold and seven-fold symmetry when visualized by electron microscopy and X-ray crystallography (Rosenberg et al., 2006).
evidence: Stated with citation to Rosenberg et al., 2006.

claim: Crystal structures of isolated hub domain assemblies of CaMKII revealed both tetradecameric and dodecameric forms.
source: Crystal structures of isolated hub domain assemblies of CaMKII revealed both tetradecameric and dodecameric forms, and spectroscopic studies provided evidence for variability in the number of subunits in intact holoenzymes (Hoelz et al., 2003; Rosenberg et al., 2006; Rellos et al., 2010; Nguyen et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated with multiple citations to structural studies.

claim: Unactivated CaMKII holoenzymes do not display appreciable subunit exchange.
source: We find that although unactivated CaMKII holoenzymes do not display appreciable subunit exchange, activation by Ca2+/CaM leads to significant subunit exchange.
evidence: Main finding stated in the introduction.

claim: Activation by Ca2+/CaM leads to significant subunit exchange in CaMKII.
source: We find that although unactivated CaMKII holoenzymes do not display appreciable subunit exchange, activation by Ca2+/CaM leads to significant subunit exchange.
evidence: Main finding stated in the introduction.

claim: Gel filtration results are consistent with the purified protein being a dodecameric form of CaMKII that has not been activated.
source: Gel filtration results are consistent with the purified protein being a dodecameric form of CaMKII that has not been activated.
evidence: Stated as a characterization of the purified protein.

claim: Mass spectrometric analysis documented that the purified CaMKII is unphosphorylated prior to activation.
source: Mass spectrometric analysis documented that the purified CaMKII is unphosphorylated prior to activation (data not shown).
evidence: Stated as a characterization of the purified protein.

claim: Gel filtration analysis of a constitutively active mutant (CaMKIIT286D) shows no evidence for aggregation.
source: Gel filtration analysis of a constitutively active mutant (CaMKIIT286D) shows no evidence for aggregation, and incubation of the wild-type holoenzyme with Ca2+/CaM and ATP shows no changes in the UV-vis absorption spectrum (data not shown).
evidence: Stated as experimental observation.

claim: The addition of ATP to CaMKIIT286D results in a small population with sizes that are larger than that of a single holoenzyme.
source: DLS measurements indicate that the addition of ATP to CaMKIIT286D, under the conditions used in our mixing experiments, results in a small population with sizes that are larger than that of a single holoenzyme (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1 showing DLS data.

claim: There is no time-dependent change in the particle size distribution over the time scale of the experiments for both wild-type CaMKII and CaMKIIT286D.
source: The DLS data for both wild-type CaMKII and CaMKIIT286D demonstrate that there is no time-dependent change in the particle size distribution over the time scale of our experiments.
evidence: Stated as a result from DLS measurements.

claim: At 37°C, the unactivated sample shows only a low level of exchange even at long time points.
source: At 37°C, the unactivated sample (i.e., with no addition of Ca2+/CaM and ATP) shows only a low level of exchange even at long time points (green).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Decreasing the concentration of CaMKII from 8 µM to 1 µM results in reduction of the rate of colocalization under activating conditions.
source: Under activating conditions, decreasing the concentration of CaMKII from 8 µM (red) to 1 µM (blue) results in reduction of the rate of colocalization.
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Activated wild-type CaMKII reaches 40% of maximal colocalization within 6 min at 37°C.
source: For example, activated wild-type CaMKII reaches 40% of maximal colocalization within 6 min at 37°C, but at 25°C the time taken to achieve the same degree of colocalization is ∼250 min.
evidence: Stated as a quantitative result from the experiments.

claim: At 25°C, activated wild-type CaMKII takes approximately 250 min to achieve 40% of maximal colocalization.
source: For example, activated wild-type CaMKII reaches 40% of maximal colocalization within 6 min at 37°C, but at 25°C the time taken to achieve the same degree of colocalization is ∼250 min.
evidence: Stated as a quantitative result from the experiments.

claim: If the concentration of CaMKII subunits is reduced from 8 μM to 1 μM, the extent of colocalization in 10 min at 37°C is reduced from ∼20% of maximal to ∼10%.
source: If the concentration of CaMKII subunits is reduced from 8 μM to 1 μM, the extent of colocalization in 10 min at 37°C is reduced from ∼20% of maximal to ∼10% (Figure 2C).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: The concentration of CaMKII subunits in dendritic spines is estimated to be ∼100 μM.
source: The concentration of CaMKII subunits in dendritic spines is estimated to be ∼100 μM (Otmakhov and Lisman, 2012), suggesting that in this environment the timescale of subunit exchange may be substantially shorter than seen in our experiments.
evidence: Stated with citation to Otmakhov and Lisman, 2012.

claim: Once CaMKII is activated, its subunits are capable of multiple cycles of exchange.
source: These data indicate that once CaMKII is activated, its subunits are capable of multiple cycles of exchange.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the pre-activation experiment.

claim: The site of labeling in the wild-type protein is Cys 280.
source: Mass spectrometric analysis showed that the labeling occurs at Cys 280, in the C-terminal lobe of the kinase domain.
evidence: Stated as a result from mass spectrometry.

claim: Labeling efficiencies ranged between 20 and 40% for the wild-type protein.
source: Labeling efficiencies ranged between 20 and 40% for the wild-type protein (see 'Materials and methods'), and this is sufficient for our analysis because of the direct visualization of holoenzymes.
evidence: Stated as a characterization of the labeling procedure.

claim: The FRET signal obtained for experiments using the D335C mutant showed a marked contrast for mixed samples that were either activated by Ca2+/CaM and ATP or not.
source: The FRET signal obtained for experiments using the D335C mutant showed a marked contrast for mixed samples that were either activated by Ca2+/CaM and ATP or not.
evidence: Stated as a result from FRET experiments.

claim: There is a substantial increase in the FRET signal that occurs within minutes of mixing the two labeled species for the activated sample.
source: There is a substantial increase in the FRET signal that occurs within minutes of mixing the two labeled species for the activated sample (Figure 2—figure supplement 5B,C).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 5B,C.

claim: In the unactivated sample, there is only a modest, slow increase in the FRET signal with time.
source: In the unactivated sample (i.e., in the absence of Ca2+/CaM and ATP), there is only a modest, slow increase in the FRET signal with time, indicating that any exchange that might occur in the unactivated sample does so at a very slow rate.
evidence: Stated as a result from FRET experiments.

claim: Fusion of CaMKII to Hcp1 strongly suppresses colocalization.
source: The strong suppression of colocalization seen with the CaMKII-Hcp1 fusion protein lends further support to the idea that CaMKII holoenzymes exchange subunits upon activation.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the Hcp1 fusion experiment.

claim: Colocalization of the CaMKII-Hcp1 fusion protein is only ∼10% even after 1 hr, compared to ∼70% for the wild-type holoenzyme.
source: Colocalization of the two fluorophores is only ∼10% even after 1 hr, compared to ∼70% for the wild-type holoenzyme (Figure 3A).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: The subunits of the isolated hub domain assembly do not exchange subunits.
source: We found that the subunits of the isolated hub domain assembly do not exchange subunits (Figure 3B).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: The short-linker construct exhibits fluorophore colocalization with the same rate as full-length CaMKIIα when activated by Ca2+/CaM and ATP.
source: As shown in Figure 3C, the short-linker construct exhibits fluorophores colocalization with the same rate as full-length CaMKIIα when activated by Ca2+/CaM and ATP, indicating that the linker is not required for subunit exchange.
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: The linker is not required for subunit exchange.
source: As shown in Figure 3C, the short-linker construct exhibits fluorophores colocalization with the same rate as full-length CaMKIIα when activated by Ca2+/CaM and ATP, indicating that the linker is not required for subunit exchange.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the short-linker experiment.

claim: Introduction of the I321E mutation in the context of the short-linker construct has no effect on the rate of colocalization.
source: Introduction of the same mutation (I321E) in the context of the short-linker construct has no effect on the rate of colocalization (Figure 3C).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: The trigger for subunit exchange does not involve the disruption of the interface between the kinase domain and the hub that is seen in the structure of the autoinhibited holoenzyme.
source: This suggests that the trigger for subunit exchange does not involve the disruption of the interface between the kinase domain and the hub that is seen in the structure of the autoinhibited holoenzyme.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the I321E mutation experiment.

claim: CaMKIIT286D displays a vigorous degree of colocalization when ATP is added in the absence of Ca2+/CaM, comparable to that of the wild-type enzyme in the presence of Ca2+/CaM and ATP.
source: CaMKIIT286D displays a vigorous degree of colocalization when ATP is added in the absence of Ca2+/CaM, comparable to that of the wild-type enzyme in the presence of Ca2+/CaM and ATP (Figure 4A).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 4A.

claim: Although activation of the catalytic module is necessary for colocalization, the physical presence of Ca2+/CaM is not required.
source: These data demonstrate that although activation of the catalytic module is necessary for colocalization, the physical presence of Ca2+/CaM is not required.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the CaMKIIT286D experiment.

claim: Replacement of residues 302 to 313 in the R3 element by an arbitrary linker sequence essentially eliminated colocalization.
source: We monitored colocalization after mixing for this construct and found that colocalization was essentially eliminated (Figure 4A).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 4A.

claim: The reduction in ATP concentration and the presence of bosutinib result in suppression of colocalization.
source: As shown in Figure 4B, the reduction in ATP concentration and the presence of bosutinib result in suppression of colocalization.
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: After 30 min of mixing, the wild-type enzyme exhibits 70% of the maximal degree of colocalization, whereas under conditions where phosphorylation is inhibited the level of colocalization is only ∼20% after 30 min.
source: For example, after 30 min of mixing, the wild-type enzyme exhibits 70% of the maximal degree of colocalization, whereas under conditions where phosphorylation is inhibited the level of colocalization is only ∼20% after 30 min.
evidence: Stated as a quantitative result from the kinase inhibitor experiment.

claim: Inhibition of kinase activity suppresses colocalization for CaMKIIT286D, although to a lesser extent than for the wild-type protein.
source: As shown in Figure 4C, inhibition of kinase activity suppresses colocalization for CaMKIIT286D, although to a lesser extent than for the wild-type protein.
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: Phosphorylation at sites other than Thr 286 is also important for exchange.
source: These data indicate that phosphorylation at sites other than Thr 286 is also important for exchange, and drew attention to a possible role for Thr 305 and Thr 306 in the exchange process.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the kinase inhibitor experiment with CaMKIIT286D.

claim: Mixing experiments demonstrated substantial reduction in colocalization for both CaMKIIT286D,T305A and CaMKIIT286D,T306A individual mutations.
source: Mixing experiments demonstrated substantial reduction in colocalization for both individual mutations, although somewhat less than the reduction obtained with treatment of CaMKIIT286D with bosutinib (Figure 4C).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: Phosphorylation of both Thr 305 and Thr 306, in addition to Thr 286, is important for subunit exchange.
source: We conclude that phosphorylation of both Thr 305 and Thr 306, in addition to Thr 286, is important for subunit exchange.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the Thr 305 and Thr 306 mutation experiments.

claim: Subunits in constitutively active CaMKIIT286D can exchange with subunits from holoenzymes that have not been activated, when ATP is added.
source: The first important result is that subunits in constitutively active CaMKIIT286D can exchange with subunits from holoenzymes that have not been activated, when ATP is added (Figure 5A).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: Fusion of the hexameric protein Hcp1 to the wild-type protein reduces the rate of colocalization with CaMKIIT286D.
source: Fusion of the hexameric protein Hcp1 to the wild-type protein reduces the rate of colocalization, indicating that the unactivated CaMKII holoenzyme has to open up in some way for the exchange process to happen.
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: There is an increase in the degree of phosphorylation detected with time when CaMKIIT286D is mixed with unactivated wild-type CaMKII.
source: As shown in Figure 5B, there is an increase in the degree of phosphorylation detected with time, demonstrating that CaMKIIT286D is able to phosphorylate subunits in unactivated wild-type CaMKII.
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: CaMKIIT286D is able to phosphorylate subunits in unactivated wild-type CaMKII.
source: As shown in Figure 5B, there is an increase in the degree of phosphorylation detected with time, demonstrating that CaMKIIT286D is able to phosphorylate subunits in unactivated wild-type CaMKII.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the three-color experiment.

claim: Trans-phosphorylation of Thr 286 occurs principally within a holoenzyme.
source: It has been shown previously that trans-phosphorylation of Thr 286 occurs principally within a holoenzyme (Hanson et al., 1994; Rich and Schulman, 1998).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: Mixing CaMKIIT286D-Hcp1 with wild-type CaMKII resulted in decreased Thr 286 phosphorylation.
source: Mixing CaMKIIT286D-Hcp1 with wild-type CaMKII resulted in decreased Thr 286 phosphorylation (Figure 5B), indicating that stabilizing the activated CaMKII holoenzyme reduces the observed phosphorylation.
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: Antibody binding occurs principally in those species in which the red and green fluorophores are colocalized.
source: In the second analysis, we showed that antibody binding occurs principally in those species in which the red and green fluorophores are colocalized (Figure 5C), consistent with subunit exchange being required for the trans-phosphorylation reaction.
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 5C.

claim: The activity of CaMKIIT286D towards a peptide substrate (syntide) is only ∼20% that of activated wild-type CaMKII.
source: We found that the activity of CaMKIIT286D towards a peptide substrate (syntide, see 'Materials and methods') is only ∼20% that of activated wild-type CaMKII (data not shown).
evidence: Stated as an experimental observation.

claim: A sample containing 1 μl of activated CaMKII at 6 μM concentration exhibits a peptide phosphorylation rate of 132 units.
source: A sample containing 1 μl of activated CaMKII at 6 μM concentration exhibits a peptide phosphorylation rate of 132 units, where the units are the change in the fluorescence of resorufin in unit time (Figure 5D).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 5D.

claim: A sample containing 3 μl of unactivated CaMKII at 6 μM concentration exhibits a rate of 49 units.
source: A second sample containing 3 μl of unactivated CaMKII at the same concentration exhibits a rate of 49 units (this activity represents the futile ATP hydrolysis rate of CaMKII, also observed without peptide substrate, data not shown).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 5D.

claim: A sample consisting of 1 μl of activated CaMKII at 6 μM mixed with 3 μl of unactivated CaMKII at 6 μM exhibits a rate of 592 units.
source: A third sample consisting of 1 μl of activated CaMKII at 6 μM mixed with 3 μl of unactivated CaMKII at 6 μM exhibits a rate of 592 units.
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 5D.

claim: Activated CaMKII holoenzymes have increased the activity of the holoenzymes that had not been activated previously.
source: This suggests that activated CaMKII holoenzymes have increased the activity of the holoenzymes that had not been activated previously.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the solution kinase assay.

claim: The CaMKII holoenzyme can be thought of as being assembled from six 'vertical dimers'.
source: The CaMKII holoenzyme can be thought of as being assembled from six 'vertical dimers'. In a view that has the mid-plane of the dodecamer horizontal, these vertical dimers each contribute one hub domain to the upper ring and one to the lower ring of the hub assembly.
evidence: Stated as a conceptual description of the holoenzyme structure.

claim: The hub domain is very closely related in structure to members of the NTF2 family.
source: That the unit of exchange might be a vertical dimer is suggested by the fact that the hub domain is very closely related in structure, although not in sequence, to members of a large family of enzymes and binding proteins, such as nuclear transport factor 2 (NTF2) and ketosteroid isomerase like proteins, which we refer to as the NTF2 family (Figure 7C; Hoelz et al., 2003).
evidence: Stated with citation and reference to Figure 7C.

claim: A common quaternary structural unit within the NTF2 family corresponds to the vertical dimer in the CaMKII hub.
source: A common quaternary structural unit within the NTF2 family corresponds to the vertical dimer in the CaMKII hub.
evidence: Stated as a structural comparison.

claim: Of the top 50 unique hits in a Dali search for structures similar to the mouse CaMKIIα hub domain, 29 form dimers in the crystal lattice that are similar to the vertical CaMKII hub dimer.
source: Of the top 50 unique hits in a Dali search (Holm and Rosenstrom, 2010) for structures similar to the mouse CaMKIIα hub domain (PDB code: 1HKX), 29 form dimers in the crystal lattice that are similar to the vertical CaMKII hub dimer (Figure 7C).
evidence: Stated with citation and reference to Figure 7C.

claim: Molecular dynamics simulations provide a clear indication that the lateral interfaces in the hub assembly are more likely to be disrupted than the equatorial ones.
source: Molecular dynamics simulations provide a clear indication that the lateral interfaces in the hub assembly are more likely to be disrupted than the equatorial ones (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The internal motions of the hub can be described as rigid-body motions of individual vertical-dimer units, with alterations in the lateral dimer–dimer interfaces.
source: The internal motions of the hub can be described as rigid-body motions of individual vertical-dimer units, with alterations in the lateral dimer–dimer interfaces.
evidence: Stated as a result from molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: For comparisons across the equatorial interfaces, the rms displacements in the neighboring subunits are ∼2 Å across the ring.
source: For comparisons across the equatorial interfaces, within a vertical dimer, the rms displacements in the neighboring subunits are ∼2 Å across the ring.
evidence: Stated as a quantitative result from molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: For comparison across the lateral interfaces, the rms displacements of the neighboring subunits are as much as 6 to 10 Å for several of the interfaces.
source: In contrast, for comparison across the lateral interfaces, the rms displacements of the neighboring subunits are as much as 6 to 10 Å for several of the interfaces, consistent with the lateral interfaces being much more flexible than the equatorial ones (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is strain associated with the closed ring formed by the dodecameric hub assembly of CaMKII.
source: Further analysis of the simulation suggests that there is strain associated with the closed ring formed by the dodecameric hub assembly of CaMKII.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: The sixfold symmetry of the ring breaks down during the course of the simulation.
source: Although the hub assembly is symmetric initially, the sixfold symmetry of the ring breaks down during the course of the simulation.
evidence: Stated as a result from molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: The constraint of ring closure prevents the simultaneous optimization of all of the lateral interfaces.
source: These results suggest that the constraint of ring closure prevents the simultaneous optimization of all of the lateral interfaces.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: There is a rapid relaxation of the curvature of the ring in both trajectories of the decameric structure.
source: There is a rapid relaxation of the curvature of the ring in both trajectories.
evidence: Stated as a result from molecular dynamics simulations of the decamer.

claim: The decameric structure opens up with respect to the starting structure in both trajectories within ∼10 ns.
source: The decameric structure opens up with respect to the starting structure in both trajectories within ∼10 ns (Figure 9B).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 9B.

claim: The structures move closer to the tetradecameric form of the hub assembly.
source: The principal outward displacement occurs in the plane of the ring so that the structures move closer to the tetradecameric form of the hub assembly (PDB code: 1HKX; Figure 9B, Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 9B and Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: The relative orientations of subunits across the two internal vertical interfaces converge to a similar arrangement, with low rms displacements, both within one trajectory and between two independent trajectories.
source: The relative orientations of subunits across these two interfaces converge to a similar arrangement, with low rms displacements, both within one trajectory and between two independent trajectories (Figure 9C, bottom left, Figure 9—figure supplement 2A), and this arrangement is different from that seen in the crystal structure of the dodecamer (Figure 9C, bottom right, Figure 9—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 9C and Figure 9—figure supplement 2.

claim: This relaxation towards a specific structure suggests that there is an enthalpic contribution to the strain in the closed ring.
source: This relaxation towards a specific structure, as seen in two independent trajectories, suggests that there is an enthalpic contribution to the strain in the closed ring.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: CaMKIIα contains three arginine residues that are located deep within the hub cavity (residues 403, 423, and 439).
source: CaMKIIα contains three arginine residues that are located deep within the hub cavity (residues 403, 423, and 439).
evidence: Stated as a structural feature.

claim: These three arginine residues are highly conserved either as arginine or lysine, with three positively charged residues present in CaMKII from C. elegans, mouse, and drosophila.
source: These residues are highly conserved either as arginine or lysine, with three positively charged residues present in CaMKII from C. elegans, mouse, and drosophila.
evidence: Stated as a conservation analysis.

claim: In each of the three molecular dynamics trajectories with the docked peptide, the R3 element retains the hydrogen bonding pattern that is consistent with its incorporation into the β sheet of the hub domain.
source: In each of these trajectories the R3 element retains the hydrogen bonding pattern (right) that is consistent with its incorporation into the β sheet of the hub domain and the phosphate group maintains its proximity to the sidechain of Arg 403, suggesting that this interaction is plausible.
evidence: Stated as a result from molecular dynamics simulations with reference to Figure 10C.

claim: The phosphate group maintains its proximity to the sidechain of Arg 403 in the molecular dynamics trajectories with the docked peptide.
source: In each of these trajectories the R3 element retains the hydrogen bonding pattern (right) that is consistent with its incorporation into the β sheet of the hub domain and the phosphate group maintains its proximity to the sidechain of Arg 403, suggesting that this interaction is plausible.
evidence: Stated as a result from molecular dynamics simulations with reference to Figure 10C.

claim: The peptide stays docked onto the β3 strand of the hub domain throughout the trajectories.
source: The peptide stays docked onto the β3 strand of the hub domain throughout the trajectories, which, in turn, prevents the crack between helix αA and the β sheet from closing (Figure 10D).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 10D.

claim: The widening of the crack is coupled to changes in the disposition of the loops that make lateral contacts with the adjacent vertical dimers.
source: Notably, the widening of the crack is coupled to changes in the disposition of the loops that make lateral contacts with the adjacent vertical dimers (Figure 10D).
evidence: Stated with reference to Figure 10D.

claim: CaMKII plays a critical role in neurons as a component of the molecular networks that lead to the strengthening of synaptic connections between co-active neurons, as exhibited in long-term potentiation (LTP).
source: Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) plays a critical role in neurons, where it is a component of the molecular networks that lead to the strengthening of synaptic connections between co-active neurons, as exhibited in long-term potentiation (LTP) (Lisman et al., 2002; Coultrap and Bayer, 2012; Lisman et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: The early phases of LTP involve the activation of CaMKII and the consequent phosphorylation of downstream targets, such as the AMPA receptor and stargazin.
source: The early phases of LTP involve the activation of CaMKII and the consequent phosphorylation of downstream targets, such as the AMPA receptor and stargazin, which leads to increased ionic currents into the neuron as well the targeting of CaMKII to other proteins involved in LTP (Lisman et al., 2002; Wayman et al., 2008).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: The activation of CaMKII results in its recruitment to the NMDA receptor.
source: The activation of CaMKII, for example, results in its recruitment to the NMDA receptor, and this NMDA:CaMKII complex may contribute to the maintenance of LTP (Bayer et al., 2001; Sanhueza et al., 2011; Sanhueza and Lisman, 2013).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: CaMKII plays an essential role in modulating cardiac pacemaking and excitation-contraction coupling.
source: CaMKII also plays an essential role in modulating cardiac pacemaking and excitation-contraction coupling.
evidence: Stated as a known function of CaMKII.

claim: Several heart diseases are associated with the hyper-activation of CaMKII.
source: Several heart diseases are associated with the hyper-activation of CaMKII (Backs et al., 2009; Chelu et al., 2009; Neef et al., 2010; Rokita and Anderson, 2012).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.

claim: Subunit exchange could facilitate the recruitment of additional holoenzymes to the NMDA receptor by spreading activation to unactivated holoenzymes.
source: Subunit exchange could facilitate the recruitment of additional holoenzymes to the receptor by spreading activation to unactivated holoenzymes.
evidence: Stated as a speculation about the functional implications.

claim: Recent experiments using a CaMKII construct engineered to be a FRET reporter of its activation state indicate that the bulk of CaMKII holoenzymes in dendrites maintain their activation state for not much longer than a minute after the stimulation is withdrawn.
source: Recent experiments using a CaMKII construct engineered to be a FRET reporter of its activation state indicate that the bulk of CaMKII holoenzymes in dendrites maintain their activation state for not much longer than a minute after the stimulation is withdrawn (Takao et al., 2005).
evidence: Stated with citation to Takao et al., 2005.

claim: Localized stimulation of a neuron resulted in the translocation of CaMKII from the main body of the axon to synapses throughout the dendritic arbor for much longer times (15–40 min) after the local stimulation is stopped.
source: Interestingly, another study demonstrated that localized stimulation of a neuron resulted in the translocation of CaMKII from the main body of the axon to synapses throughout the dendritic arbor for much longer times (15–40 min) after the local stimulation is stopped; the authors of this report commented that subunit exchange may play a role in this process (Rose et al., 2009).
evidence: Stated with citation to Rose et al., 2009.

claim: Calmodulin is limiting in synapses.
source: Given the high concentrations of CaMKII in synapses and the fact that calmodulin is limiting (Liu and Storm, 1990; MacNicol and Schulman, 1992; Persechini and Stemmer, 2002), subunit exchange provides a potential mechanism for increasing the spread of activation caused by an initial activating pulse.
evidence: Stated with citations to prior studies.
